verses.text: Family, when I came to you, I didn’t roll in with a big speech or try to flex human wisdom while sharing God’s message.
I made one thing my focus among you: Jesus Christ, crucified.
I showed up weak, scared, and shaking.
My words and preaching weren’t some slick, persuasive pitch. The Spirit showed up with power.
That way, your faith wouldn’t rest on people’s wisdom, but on God’s power.
We do speak wisdom among mature believers—but it isn’t this world’s wisdom or the rulers’ wisdom. Their power is already fading out.
We speak God’s wisdom, hidden like a mystery: the wisdom he planned before time began for our glory.
The rulers of this age didn’t understand it. If they had, they wouldn’t have crucified the glorious Lord.
Scripture says, “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no human heart has imagined what God has prepared for those who love him.”
But God has revealed these things to us through the Spirit. The Spirit searches everything—even God’s deepest thoughts.
Who knows what’s going on inside a person except that person’s own spirit? In the same way, nobody knows God’s thoughts except God’s Spirit.
We didn’t receive the world’s spirit. We received the Spirit who comes from God, so we can know the gifts God freely gave us.
We talk about these things in words the Spirit teaches—not in phrases human wisdom taught us—as we explain spiritual truth to people who have the Spirit.
Someone relying only on human judgment doesn’t welcome what comes from God’s Spirit. It sounds ridiculous to them, and they can’t understand it because it takes spiritual discernment.
But the person guided by the Spirit can discern everything, and no one can put that person on trial.
“Who has known the Lord’s mind well enough to advise him?” But we have the mind of Christ. 🧠
